title: linux-omarchy: carry ACPICA PCI bus fix for resume delays
author: Clowdyffs
body:
Submitting this directly in the omarchy repo since omarchy seems to have a lot of old macbooks in its userbase. For it to change upstream it has to go through the acpica review process, the linux kernel release candidates, then the arch linux kernel has to be released after that, which could make this change take a couple months or longer (if ever). If and when it gets merged, I'll keep track of it and submit a follow up PR to remove this patch from this repo since it will be directly inherited. 

-----------everything below this line is written by ai------------


Carry the PCI operation-region address correction proposed in **https://github.com/open-acpica/acpica/pull/1235** in `linux-omarchy` and `linux-omarchy-bore`. On a MacBookPro14,1, this fixes incorrectly cached PCI addresses during resume and reduces three affected firmware sequences from **6.939 seconds to 1.836 milliseconds**.

**Upstream status:** ACPICA #1235 is open for review, not accepted or merged. This is a proposed downstream carry of its current source change, not an already accepted upstream backport. The upstream PR contains the full diagnosis, trace excerpts, historical rationale and standalone reproducer. Please keep this carry aligned with upstream review and remove it when the packaged base kernel includes the correction. Merge timing can follow that review.

## What changes

- Add the same `0771-acpica-preserve-parent-derived-pci-bus.patch` to the standard and BORE recipes, following this repository's practice of keeping shared kernel fixes in both variants.
- Update SHA-256 and BLAKE2 checksums and bump both recipes from `7.2.5-6` to `7.2.5-7`.
- The kernel diff changes only `drivers/acpi/acpica/hwpci.c`: six insertions and eleven deletions. Existing `prepare()` applies it with `--fuzz=0`; no new build logic, kernel configuration, power hook, DMI quirk or sleep-policy change is needed.

The patch links to the upstream PR and identifies its human-signed source commit, [`615f1b568156`](https://github.com/open-acpica/acpica/commit/615f1b568156cf6a58040839f4ade773d8da7cf9). Its existing author sign-off and AI-assistance disclosure are preserved. Paths, identifiers and the `Fixes:` reference are translated to Linux form; the functional correction is unchanged.

## Root cause and why it should be corrected

`acpi_hw_get_pci_device_info()` locates each bridge using the bus derived from its parent. It then reads that bridge's Primary Bus Number register and overwrites the already established address before reading the Secondary Bus Number.

During this machine's ACPI power-up, the bridge header is accessible before the PCI core has restored the bridge's bus-number registers. The primary register can still contain its reset value, zero. The captured upstream bridge is at `04:00.0`, but its primary register reads zero; the overwrite redirects the next configuration read to host bridge `00:00.0`. Derivation nevertheless returns `AE_OK`, and the operation region retains the wrong address. The downstream bridge shows the same mechanism.

Consequently, the firmware mailbox region at offset `0x530` directs **150,120 polling reads to the host bridge**, instead of the intended Thunderbolt bridge. Associated accesses at `0x538` and writes are likewise misdirected. Three firmware retry sequences exhaust their counters. Leaving this unchanged retains incorrect address derivation and misdirected configuration accesses, as well as the visible delay. No host-bridge corruption, exploit or security-boundary crossing was demonstrated.

The correction retains the parent-derived address and removes the redundant primary-register read. It preserves device/header checks and secondary-bus reads/error handling. It changes neither firmware retry limits nor PCI power sequencing, and removes one configuration read per inspected bridge rather than adding polling or delays.

The code originated in ACPICA [`08fd52445bf4`](https://github.com/open-acpica/acpica/commit/08fd52445bf4cfb28e2b66b77866e43ab8ade6d2), imported into Linux as [`95abccb576c4`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/95abccb576c44bc593e05fa1245d0ad26ce6107b). The patch uses the Linux commit in its `Fixes:` tag.

## Hardware evidence and performance

Tested hardware: **MacBookPro14,1**, 2017 13-inch Intel MacBook Pro, two Thunderbolt 3 ports, no Touch Bar; firmware **451.120.7.0.0**, Alpine Ridge controller **8086:1578**.

The controlled stock/corrected comparison used Linux **7.2.3-arch1-3** with the same temporary Thunderbolt LC-skip protection and `pm_test=platform`. These automatic-return diagnostic transitions include a deliberate five-second pause and do **not** enter actual sleep.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Three affected CRMW firmware sequences combined | 6.939 s | 1.836 ms |
| Complete diagnostic transition, including the five-second pause | 15.550 s | 8.106 s |

The affected firmware sequences save approximately **6.937 seconds (99.97% shorter)**. This percentage is **not a total-system wake speedup**. All six mailbox CIOR calls succeeded after correction, and traced operation-region addresses matched the actual bridge addresses. Later combined real-sleep tests also succeeded, but included separate controller protection and therefore do not establish that this patch alone fixes suspend.

The machine currently runs the official `linux-omarchy 7.2.5-3`; the source recipe targeted here is `7.2.5-6`. The corrected 7.2.3 kernel was built and booted earlier. These are distinct from a new build or hardware test of this packaging PR.

## Scope and compatibility limits

This is a generic ACPICA correctness change, not a Mac-specific workaround. ACPICA serves other hardware and operating systems, so **one MacBook cannot establish universal safety**. Restored bridges should retain the same addresses because the primary register normally agrees with the parent-derived bus. Other firmware/topology behavior still needs upstream review and broader testing.

The expanded reproducer compiles the actual C helper and passes **15 cases**: four corrected failures and eleven unchanged comparisons. Coverage includes ordinary bridges/endpoints, namespace scopes, nonzero root buses and CardBus headers. The nonzero-root/CardBus additions are simulated fixtures, not physical-device coverage; the patch does not reconstruct an unavailable ancestor secondary-bus value. No universal no-regression claim is made, and BORE has not been boot-tested here.

The separate Thunderbolt power-transition/controller-loss fault can still produce the xHCI **65,535 ms timeout** with this address fix present. A corrected-kernel stock-driver control reproduced that fault while the three firmware sequences remained fast (2.675 ms). This PR therefore does not claim to resolve the full minute-long wake, lid wake delivery, sleep power consumption, or intermittent BCM4350 Wi-Fi failure.

Related controller work: https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/10593, https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/10758 and #349. This carry is separate from those driver/state-restoration changes and should not close their reports.

## Validation

- Both PKGBUILDs pass `bash -n` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`; source/checksum array lengths and all checked-in hashed sources, including architecture configs, match.
- The two patch copies are byte-identical. No other patch in either recipe touches `drivers/acpi/acpica/hwpci.c`.
- The carry applies to the exact Linux **v7.2.5** helper with **zero fuzz and zero offset**. The resulting file is byte-identical to the previously validated Linux-form correction.
- The actual-C **15-case replay passes against that v7.2.5 result**, compiled with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`. The complete reproducible harness is in ACPICA #1235.
- Strict Linux `checkpatch.pl`: **zero errors, warnings or checks**. `git diff --check` passes for both recipes and for the resulting kernel-source diff (the outer diff of a new `.patch` file naturally contains unified-diff context markers).
- `bin/build-matrix linux-omarchy linux-omarchy-bore` selects both x86_64 edge builds.
- Previously completed validation: native ACPICA `acpiexec`/`acpisrc` build, the equivalent corrected Linux 7.2.3 kernel build/boot, and the hardware comparison above.

A full build of the new 7.2.5 package recipes, full patch-stack application and new hardware/BORE boot testing have **not** been performed locally. Existing remote archive/signature inputs are unchanged and were not downloaded/reverified for these targeted checks. The repository's normal package build/review remains necessary before shipping.

@@ -0,0 +1,75 @@
+From: clowdyffs <alex@clowdydev.com>
+Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 20:55:46 -0400
+Subject: [PATCH] ACPICA: Preserve the parent-derived PCI bus when inspecting bridges
+
+A PCI_Config operation region first used during a bridge's ACPI power-up
+can be initialized before the PCI core restores that bridge's bus-number
+registers. acpi_hw_get_pci_device_info() has already located the bridge
+using its parent's secondary bus. Reading a zero Primary Bus Number and
+assigning it to pci_id->bus then misdirects the following secondary-bus
+read and caches the wrong region address.
+
+On MacBookPro14,1, first-resume tracing records UPSB at 04:00.0 with
+header type 1 and primary bus 0. Region derivation returns 00:00.0
+successfully. The H530 region then directs 150,120 mailbox polls to the
+host bridge; three exhausted firmware retry sequences cost about seven
+seconds. Two downstream-bridge regions show the same address loss.
+
+Keep the address already derived from the parent and remove the
+unnecessary primary-bus read. The secondary-bus read then uses that same
+correct bridge address. This changes neither the PCI power sequence nor
+firmware retry limits.
+
+Hardware validation on MacBookPro14,1 confirms correct PCI region
+addresses and successful mailbox access: the three firmware retry
+sequences fell from 6.939 seconds to 1.836 milliseconds. A replay of the
+actual C helper also corrects two captured reset-primary cases and
+preserves six comparison cases.
+
+A separate Thunderbolt controller power-transition failure still occurs
+with this correction. This change fixes PCI region address derivation.
+
+Fixes: 95abccb576c4 ("ACPICA: Obsolete the acpi_os_derive_pci_id OSL interface")
+Link: https://github.com/open-acpica/acpica/pull/1235
+Assisted-by: LLM
+Signed-off-by: clowdyffs <alex@clowdydev.com>
+---
+Linux-form carry of ACPICA commit 615f1b568156cf6a58040839f4ade773d8da7cf9.
+Upstream PR #1235 is pending review, not accepted or merged. Update this
+carry with upstream review and drop it once the base kernel includes the fix.
+The author sign-off above is preserved from the upstream submission.
+
+diff --git a/drivers/acpi/acpica/hwpci.c b/drivers/acpi/acpica/hwpci.c
+--- a/drivers/acpi/acpica/hwpci.c
++++ b/drivers/acpi/acpica/hwpci.c
+@@ -13,7 +13,6 @@
+ 
+ /* PCI configuration space values */
+ #define PCI_CFG_HEADER_TYPE_REG             0x0E
+-#define PCI_CFG_PRIMARY_BUS_NUMBER_REG      0x18
+ #define PCI_CFG_SECONDARY_BUS_NUMBER_REG    0x19
+ /* PCI header values */
+ #define PCI_HEADER_TYPE_MASK                0x7F
+@@ -358,17 +357,13 @@
+ 		return (AE_OK);
+ 	}
+ 
+-	/* Bridge: Get the Primary bus_number */
+-
+-	status = acpi_os_read_pci_configuration(pci_id,
+-						PCI_CFG_PRIMARY_BUS_NUMBER_REG,
+-						&pci_value, 8);
+-	if (ACPI_FAILURE(status)) {
+-		return (status);
+-	}
+-
++	/*
++	 * Keep the bus derived from the parent bridge. The Primary Bus Number
++	 * register may still contain its reset value when a region is first
++	 * accessed during resume, before the PCI core restores bridge state.
++	 * Replacing the derived bus would also misdirect the following read.
++	 */
+ 	*is_bridge = TRUE;
+-	pci_id->bus = (u16)pci_value;
+ 
+ 	/* Bridge: Get the Secondary bus_number */
